description:
Problem: oracle-verdict.yml runs each review as a chain of jobs: plan, select-1, attempt-1-omp, then select-N and attempt-N-omp for retries up to max_attempts 5, then post (.github/workflows/oracle-verdict.yml:60-1013). Every job waits for a runner in the organisation's 20-job GitHub Free pool. Measured on 2026-10-25 from the jobs API: #3463 run 40200327188 and #3467 run 40200347117 each spent about 2h15m queueing for about 4 minutes of work (plan 9-14 min, select-1 36-39, attempt-1 26-31, select-2 26-36, post 25-28), creation to posted verdict 2h20m51s and 2h13m31s. The chain was built in #2686 (0e5123270, 2026-10-05) so each reviewer CLI held only its own provider key; the 2026-10-22 gateway decision removed provider keys from runners, so attempt jobs now isolate identical credentials.

Outcome: one review job per verdict run (option C of the 2026-10-25 job-boundary analysis): checkout trusted develop copy, check out the PR head as read-only data, plan, classify, C4 scan, install and verify OMP, join the tailnet, run the attempt loop as one CLI command, finalize, C5 re-sanitise, mint the App token, guard and post, upload attempt and retry-state artifacts, dispatch oracle-gate. Queue admissions per verdict fall from 5 (first-attempt decision) or up to 11 (five attempts) to 1, plus the unchanged oracle-gate admission.

Threat model (owner decision 2026-10-25): the reviewer is an untrusted model inside a trusted harness with read-only tools. It can read what the runner user can read while it runs and can leak it only through its published review text; it cannot write, execute or persist processes. So a secret is safe if it exists only in the environment of a step that ends before the reviewer starts, is never written to disk, or appears only after the reviewer exits; any step after the reviewer exits is trustworthy.

Preserved behaviour: the review job's if: condition equals the current plan job's (pull_request_target except plain edits, issue_comment /oracle-review from owners, members and collaborators, workflow_dispatch); every attempt leaves a result file even when the reviewer crashes or times out, as ensure-attempt guarantees today (oracle-verdict.yml:259-263); attempt and retry-state artifacts keep their names and 7-day retention and are uploaded after the loop. No required status context names an oracle-verdict job (develop ruleset 15611785 requires core, explorer, results-data, docs, tooling, hold and oracle-gate; read 2026-10-25), so removing the chain's jobs changes no required check.

Required controls, each a permanent automated check (from the second Advisor review of 2026-10-25):
- C2 total exit: after each reviewer exit the harness process group and the harness PID's descendants are empty; otherwise kill them and fail the review closed. runner.execute kills the group only on timeout today (_project/scripts/oracle_reviewers/runner.py:81-98).
- C3 no secret in a script: no run: block interpolates secrets.* or github.token; secrets reach steps only through env: or action with:.
- C4 disk scan: after classification and again after the loop, scan $HOME, $RUNNER_TEMP and both checkouts for the exact TypeSafe key and job token values; fail closed on a hit.
- C5 redaction completeness: after the loop, a trusted step holding every secret value the job held (ORACLE_GATEWAY_TOKEN, TYPESAFE_API_KEY, ORACLE_GATEWAY_URL, TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, TS_AUDIENCE, ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN, the job token) redacts attempt, verdict, diagnostic and absence text and fails closed if any value remains in clear or control-split form. The loop step itself must not hold those extra values, because a same-user child can read its parent's /proc environ.
- C6 fresh HOME per attempt: each attempt gets a new scratch HOME written by reviewer-home; the previous one is deleted before the next attempt.
- C7 token scope: job permissions are exactly actions: write, contents: read, pull-requests: read, id-token: write; github.token appears only in env: of steps that finish before the first reviewer starts or run after the final exit check; both checkouts use persist-credentials: false.
- C8 timeout budget: job timeout-minutes is computed from the policy as max_attempts x largest reviewer timeout_minutes + setup allowance, under 360; the harness per-attempt timeout still fires first.
- C9 cancellation: the top-level concurrency expression and cancel-in-progress are unchanged (oracle-verdict.yml:23-25); a cancelled run posts nothing.
- C10 App mint last: the only step referencing ORACLE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY runs after the final exit check and C5.
C1 (a sentinel canary on a hosted runner) is dropped by owner decision 2026-10-25 (skip the canary); C2-C10 stay as permanent checks instead.

Redaction decisions (owner 2026-10-25): ORACLE_GATEWAY_URL is sensitive and joins the redaction names (_project/scripts/oracle_reviewers/credentials.py:10-21); the OIDC request token is accepted within the reviewer's read reach, like the gateway token, relying on GitHub's documented rule that it is valid only while the job runs, and its value is redacted. No probe.

Decision gates:
1. Before any edit, record in context the current job graph, per-job permissions and develop SHA, and diff them against this description (own-edit-target freshness). If oracle-verdict.yml changed shape, update this item first.
2. Shape fallback: if any of C2-C10 cannot be made to pass on GitHub-hosted runners (in PR CI or in the first five live runs), implement option D instead: the same review job plus a separate post job holding the App key, consuming uploaded artifacts. Record which check failed and why in context and in the decision record. Stop and ask only if D also fails a check.
3. Merge timing (owner 2026-10-25): merge when ready, even inside the sweep items' measurement window; leave the sweep job and concurrency untouched and record the cutover.
4. Live regression: if a live run after merge fails to post a verdict that the old chain would have posted, open a revert PR first, then fix forward.

Item guardrails: do not change selection logic (selection.py), policy values, retry budget, daily budget or backoff, the sweep job, the on: triggers, the concurrency expression, oracle-gate.yml, the App binding or ruleset, review and comment formats, carry and patch-hash logic, oracle-verdict-state-<pr> and attempt artifact names or formats (except added redaction), the reviewer environment allowlist (gateway token only), or the OMP pin. No settings, secrets, environment or ruleset edits. The PR head checkout is data and is never executed.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. Never use git stash (refs/stash is shared across worktrees). Commit as Joe Harris <joeharris76@gmail.com>, staging explicit paths only; no git add -A, no --no-verify, no SKIP, no agent trailers. Durable text (commits, PR bodies, docs, comments) carries no tracker ids, session labels or plan references. Maintained code has no explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check). Run make docs-reference-inventory-check and make doc-contracts-guard in addition to make pr-preflight. Close out with make pr-open, oracle SHIP on the exact head, make pr-arm; never raw gh pr merge, never a stand-in or bypass on these oracle soundness paths.
